MRI of left Knee with 
-3-Plane Loc, Sag PD FS, Sag T2 FS, Sag T1, Ax T2 FS, Cor T2 FS

> There are linear signal intensity in posterior horn of medial meniscus, it extends into the surface, in favor of tear.
> Linear signal intensity in posterior horn of lateral meniscus, without significant extending into the surface, in favor of  grade 2 intrasubstance signal of posterior horn of medial meniscus, maybe due to degeneration.
> The contour of ACL & PCL appear to be within normal, no abnormal signal intensity is noted.
> Both medial & lateral collateral ligaments appear to be within normal.
> Joint effusion and suprapatellar bursitis with suprapatellar and medial plicae; hypertrophy of the synovium, indicative of synovitis.
> Mild heterogenous singla intensity of paterllar cartilage, in favor of grade 1-2 chondromalacia.
> Wearing of articular cartilage of left knee, major at medial compartment with spur formation and mild subchondral edema, reflecting osteoarthritis.
> Lobulated hyperintensity foci located below proximal tibiofibular joint abutting popliteal tendon/ muscle, R/O bursitis.

Impression: 
1. Osteoarthritis of left knee with synovitis.
2. C/W tear of posterior horn of medial meniscus.
3. Grade 1-2 patellar chondromalacia.
4. R/O bursitis along popliteal tendon.
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation

Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Left knee pain 10 months associated with jumping and activity. History of prior injection.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture. Minimal focal increased T2 signal peripheral lateral femoral condyle may reflect resolving low grade osseous contusion. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
No joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Trace Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: Focal partial-thickness cartilage loss along the central weightbearing medial femoral condyle.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Heterogeneity at the median ridge compatible with low grade cartilage loss. No focal high grade cartilage defects.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: Moderate distal quadriceps insertional tendinosis with superimposed edema of the retroquadriceps fat and low-grade interstitial tearing of the posterior lateral insertional fibers. Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 14 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	Moderate distal quadriceps insertional tendinosis with low-grade partial-thickness tear of the posterior lateral insertional fibers.
2.	Minimal bone marrow edema peripheral lateral femoral condyle, may reflect resolving low grade osseous contusion. 
3.	Mild patellofemoral and medial tibiofemoral compartment chondrosis.

Diz eklemi içi sıvı miktarı orta derecede artmış. Medyal femorotibyal eklemdeki hafif dereceli osteoartrit femoral kondilin ağırlık taşıyan yüzeyindeki kondral kalınlığın %50'sini  aşmayan incelme ve milimetrik fokal tam kat kondral fissürler ile karakterize. Femoral kondil medyali ve tibyal platoda lateralde kemik iliği ödemi izleniyor. Medyal menisküs arka boynuzu - gövdesindeki  dejenerasyonu arka kökü düzeyindeki tam kata ulaşmayan vertikal yırtık eşlik ediyor. İç yan bağın çevresi ödemli. Medyal menisküs medyale 3.5 mm ekstrüzyon gösteriyor. Lateral menisküs normal. Gastroknemyus-semimembranozus bursasındaki 4.7 cm maksimum boyutlu içerisinde debriyi telkin eden düşük intensiteli alanlar gözlenen sıvı lokülasyonunun çevresindeki yumuşak  doku ödemi sızdırdığını telkin ediyor. Diz ekleminin anteriyorunda prepateller - yüzeyel infrapateller cilt altı bağ dokusu ödemli. Çapraz ve yan bağlar bunların dışında normal. Medyal patellar sinovyal plika kalınlığı normal olup eklem aralığına interpoze değil. Hoffa'nın yağ yastıkçığı ödemli. Ekstensör mekanizma korunmuş. Proksimal tibyofibular eklem normal.

CLINICAL HISTORY:Left knee injury fall, <[YEAR]>.

PROCEDURE:Multisequence, multiplanar unenhanced MRI of the left knee according to routine protocol.

IMAGING FINDINGS:

Nondiagnostic scout localizing images reviewed.

Diminutive horn of the lateral meniscus consistent with complex tear. The lateral meniscal body and posterior horn show intrasubstance degeneration without additional tear. No lateral meniscal extrusion. The medial meniscus shows intrasubstance degeneration and slight peripheral extrusion of the body, without tear.

Intact anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate ligament. Small insertional cysts at the anterior cruciate ligament foot plate.

The medial collateral ligament and posterior oblique ligament are intact. The fibular collateral ligament is intact. Mild popliteus tendinosis without tear. Biceps femoris tendon insertion is intact. Iliotibial band is intact.

Attenuated appearance of the medial patellofemoral ligament suggestive of prior tear. Slight lateral patellar subluxation. The lateral patellar retinaculum is intact. No femoral trochlear dysplasia. The TT-TG distance measures 12 mm, within normal limits. The quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact.

Foci of full-thickness cartilage denuding patellar apex, lateral patellar facet, as well as central to lateral femoral trochlea. There is fissuring of articular cartilage throughout the lateral femorotibial compartment. There is mild to moderate medial femorotibial chondrosis.

Trace knee joint fluid. Small Baker's cyst. Regional musculature is within normal limits. No suspicious focal marrow signal alteration. 

IMPRESSION:
1. Complex tear anterior horn lateral meniscus without lateral meniscal extrusion.
2. Popliteus tendinosis without tear.
3. Suspected prior tear of the medial patellofemoral ligament with only slight lateral patellar subluxation.
4. Tricompartment chondrosis most pronounced involving the patellofemoral compartment consistent with moderate to severe patellofemoral predominant tricompartment osteoarthritis of the left knee.
